- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent periods.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive declines), model overreacts; dampen forecast by 1–4% to align with trend.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history includes recent positive spikes (e.g., 0.4–0.6), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
